headline: Gulf Missiles Rattle Monday Open as Oil Surges and Chips Reel
body_html:
Investors arrive at their desks Monday morning navigating a sharply deteriorated geopolitical backdrop after an active weekend of military exchanges in the Middle East. Iran launched strikes against two U.S. bases in Jordan, while U.S. forces retaliated by hitting Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island in the Persian Gulf. Crude oil is climbing on the news, and early risk-off sentiment is pressing equity futures lower heading into the open.

The mood sours an already fragile picture established during Friday's session, when decliners outnumbered advancers by nearly two to one — 353 down against 194 up across our 549-name universe. Semiconductors were the week's sharpest casualty, with the sector shedding 3.49% as a group. Marvell Technology alone fell more than 10%, with Semtech, Vicor, FormFactor, and Onto Innovation each dropping between 7% and 8% on the same day.

At the open, watch the energy complex closely: Schlumberger gained 4.22% on Friday, and oilfield-services names could extend further as oil prices climb. Treasury yields remain elevated, a headwind for growth and software names that were already slipping. The first catalyst of substance arrives with the Monday ISM Manufacturing print, which could set the directional tone if geopolitical noise briefly fades.

briefs.headline: Iran-U.S. Strikes Escalate Across the Gulf Region
briefs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards confirmed launching attacks on two U.S. military installations in Jordan over the weekend. U.S. forces responded by striking Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island in the Persian Gulf. Tehran has since vowed a further response, keeping risk assets on edge as the new trading week begins.

briefs.headline: Oil Jumps as Kharg Island Tensions Mount
briefs.body: Crude futures are rising sharply after conflicting reports emerged over the status of Iran's Kharg Island, a critical petroleum export hub. President Trump claimed the facility had suffered serious damage, a characterization Iran flatly denied. The uncertainty alone is driving a precautionary bid in oil markets ahead of Monday's open.

briefs.headline: U.S. Treasury Signals Broadening Iran Sanctions Campaign
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent indicated the administration plans to roll out fresh secondary sanctions targeting Iran on a weekly cadence, intensifying economic pressure alongside the military exchanges. The move signals a sustained, multi-front campaign that could further disrupt regional energy flows and supply-chain confidence in coming weeks.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Faces Renewed Pressure at the Open
briefs.body: Friday's session left semiconductors as the week's worst-performing sector, off 3.49% as a group. Marvell Technology, Semtech, and several equipment names each shed more than 7%, and the geopolitical overhang entering Monday is unlikely to provide relief for a complex already absorbing demand concerns.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders and Apparel Led Friday's Narrow Bright Spots
briefs.body: Against a broadly negative tape, homebuilders managed a 0.85% sector gain on Friday, the best showing across the universe. Gap Inc. surged nearly 13% to top all advancers, while specialty-materials firm Solstice Advanced Materials added close to 13% as well, suggesting selective demand persisted even as the wider market softened.

briefs.headline: Asian Equities Retreat as Oil Climbs and Yields Hold Firm
briefs.body: Regional share markets in Asia traded cautiously to start the week, with investors weighing rising oil prices against persistently elevated sovereign yields. Indian equities faced an additional overhang from a scheduled MSCI index rebalancing, adding a layer of flow-driven uncertainty on top of the broader geopolitical unease.
